2.w: “Hear, O wise men, my words, and give ear to me, knowing ones.

3.w: For the ear shall test words, and the palate tastes to eat.

4.w: Let us choose for ourselves what is just; let us know among ourselves what [is] good.

5.w: For Job has said, ‘I am righteous, and God has turned aside my justice.

6.w: [And] over my justice should I lie? Mortal [is] my arrow, without transgression.’

7.w: Who [is] a man like Job, drinking up derision like the water,

8.w: and he travels in company with workers of iniquity, and in walking with men of wickedness?

9.w: For he has said, ‘Nothing does it profit a man that he should delight in God.’

10.w: Therefore, O men of heart, listen to me. Far be it to God from wickedness, and Shaddai from injustice.

11.w: For the work of man, he repays to him; and according to the way of a man, He causes him to find [it].

12.w: Yes, surely God does not act wickedly, and Shaddai does not pervert justice.

13.w: Who gave charge to Him over the earth? And who has set [Him] [over] all of the world?

14.w: If He should set His heart to it, gathering His Spirit and His breath to Himself,

15.w: [then] all flesh would perish together, and man would return to the dust.

16.w: And if [there is] understanding, hear this; give ear to the sound of my words.

17.w: And shall one hating justice govern? Or will you declare wicked the just and mighty One?

18.w: Who says to a king, ‘Worthless,’ [or] to nobles, ‘Wicked’?

19.w: Who does not lift the faces of princes, and does not acknowledge the rich before the face of the poor, for they [are] all the work of His hands.

20.w: [In] a moment they die, and in the middle of the night the people are shaken and pass away; and the mighty are taken away, not by a hand.

21.w: For His eyes [are] upon the ways of man, and all of his steps He sees.

22.w: There is no darkness and no shadow of death, [for] the workers of iniquity to be hidden there.

23.w: For He does not set upon a man further, for his going before God in the judgment.

24.w: He breaks the mighty without investigation, and makes others stand in their place.

25.w: Therefore, He recognizes their works, and He overturns [them] in the night, and they are crushed.

26.w: In exchange for their wickednesses, He strikes them in a place of seeing,

27.w: which [was] upon thus: They turned aside from Him, and they had no regard for any of His ways,

28.w: They caused the cry of the poor to cause to come before Him—and He heard the cry of the afflicted.

29.w: And he is silent, and who can call Him wicked? And He hides [His] face, and who can see Him? And He is over a nation and over man alike,

30.w: from the reigning of godless a man, from the snares of the people.

31.w: If one says to God, ‘I have lifted [it], [and] no more will I offend;

32.w: besides what I see, You teach me; if I have done iniquity, I will not continue [it]’

33.w: will he repay it from with you, because you have rejected [it]? Then you must choose, and not I, and may you speak what you know.

34.w: Men of understanding will say to me, and the wise man [who is] listening to me:

35.w: ‘Job [does] not speak with knowledge, and His words [are] not with wisdom.’

36.w: If only Job were tested to the end, upon his answers among men of iniquity!

37.w: For he adds rebellion upon his sin; among us he claps, and he multiplies his words against God.”
